name: Stereo width: Haas, mid/side, detune, short-IR and mono-safe widening
goal: Widen sounds without phase problems: asymmetric L/R processing, Haas delays with phase offsets, short-IR wideners, band-split widening (highs wide, lows mono), chord-split panning and stereo filter/ladder spread.

sources.title: 12 Ways To Widen Your Sounds Like A Pro
Principles of Mixing 38 - Stereo Widening with Haas Effect and Phase
3 Stereo Width Tricks (That Sound Great In Mono)
Get A Wide Mix Without Any Issues!

theory: Width comes from L/R differences (time, pitch, filtering). Correlation near +1 = mono, 0 = wide, negative = cancellation risk. Haas delays (5-30 ms) widen but comb-filter in mono.
prerequisites: Auto-pan / drawable pan LFO; multiband splitter; short L/R delay
Convolution reverb with short room IRs (Web Audio: ConvolverNode with a short stereo IR, implementation note)
DAW/Web Audio graph with per-channel (L/R) EQ, saturation, delay and a parallel rack/splitter
Pad that sounds good but narrow; for A: multiband pan or band-split + auto-pan; for B: DAW that can duplicate instrument+MIDI and a pad with multi-note chords; correlation/phase meter
Stereo tool or delay with independent L/R delay offset; all-pass/phase-offset per channel (any 'stereo shaper' style plugin or Web Audio DelayNode + BiquadFilter allpass); mono-sum monitoring

outputs.name: result
outputs.description: Rendered part or recipe following the workflow

constraints: Portable recipe; not affiliated with any vendor; do not copy factory presets or sample packs.
Numbers in variants come from the source video transcripts; workflow steps are the consolidated mainstream practice.
Bring drums in early and avoid pitch wobble unless asked (user preferences from daily tests).

steps.action: Prefer decorrelation: slight detune, different LFO phases, different filter cutoffs or chord notes split L/R.
Haas: 5-20 ms on one side, automate amount; check mono sum.
Mid/side: widen only the high band; short-IR widener with width trim.
Measure correlation; back off if it goes negative.
Hear the theory: run `/home/box/audio-tools/bin/python sample-lab/theory/stereo_width.py` from the repo root and compare the sections; reuse its functions as a starting point for renders.
steps.expect: WAV in sample-lab/theory/out/ demonstrating the principle

verification: Render a short test and A/B against a reference at matched loudness
Run the generator and confirm it writes a WAV without error
Check mono compatibility and that no element masks the kick/bass

variants.name: Width by processing left and right differently (L/R EQ, one-sided saturation, formant shift, slap times) with a mono-safe parallel blend
variants.goal: Widen synths, pads and FX by making the left and right channels genuinely different - double-tracked or alternate sources hard-panned, different L/R EQ, saturation on only one side, a formant-shifted duplicate on one side, and a short slap delay at different times per side (about 50 vs 75 ms) - and blend any phase-risky width (Haas/width plus distortion) in parallel beside an untouched dry chain so mono compatibility is preserved; delta beyond the existing Haas, mid/side and unison skills.
steps: Most organic: make L and R different sources - record an analog synth part twice, or use two different claps/variants - and hard-pan one left and one right.
L/R EQ: EQ each side differently (e.g. brighter left; right with highs reduced and mids boosted).
Mid/side EQ only helps if the sound already has side content (a single mono output has none): boost sides more than mid.

Parallel width chain: keep a dry chain untouched and add a second chain with a Haas/width effect followed by distortion; mix the wet chain in slowly until width appears while mono compatibility stays good.
Saturate only one side (pan the drive to the right, leaving the left clean).
Chorus as the old-school widener for mono synths - note it can sterilise the tone.

Haas via delay (widest but sacrifices phase integrity): one side ~1 ms, the other ~6-20 ms, low feedback, EQ the delay; reserve it for supplemental pads/layers and avoid stacking it on already-reverbed/delayed sounds.
Formant-shift one duplicate and leave the other unshifted, panned apart.
Slap delay return: about 50 ms on one side and 75 ms on the other (tape-style delay preferred), feedback to taste - cleaner and less unnatural than Haas.

Synth-side: two otherwise identical saws with a different waveform variant on one, panned L/R with the random(-phase) control turned down; or unison with per-voice pan and fine detune; or pan different filters per side; reverb also adds width.
Check the mono sum after each method and back off the risky ones first.

variants.name: Haas delay + per-channel phase offset width, automated, with mono check
variants.goal: Widen a mono synth or pad without panning by combining a small inter-channel delay (Haas range, kept under ~20 ms and often below 15 ms) with a filter-based phase offset on one channel (more mono compatible because it only shifts some frequencies), then automate the width on and off for drops/sections and always confirm in mono that comb filtering is acceptable.
steps: Start with the mono source through a stereo tool set to pass-through; confirm it is centered.
Add a delay between left and right. Large offsets are heard as an echo; stay in Haas range (≤ ~20 ms, and for some sounds even 15 ms is noticeable) so it reads as width/position instead.
Sum to mono: time offsets cause comb filtering (static phaser-like coloration). Reduce the delay or skip the effect if the mono sum sounds hollow or wrong.
Add phase offset (filter-based phase shift) to one channel instead of, or with, the delay; it only moves some frequencies so it is more mono compatible.
Combine a small phase shift with a small delay shift (try either direction) to place the sound wide and out of the way of centered kick/snare; as an alternative to panning it stays on both sides.
Automate the widener: off for verses, on (or wider) when a drop hits, or sweep from wide to mono for contrast.
Before rendering, do a final mono check of the full mix.

variants.name: Widen a pad without phase smear: high-band pan LFO or hard-panned chord split
variants.goal: Widen a narrow pad without chorus/imager/spreader phase damage using one of two portable methods: (A) multiband-pan only the high band with a slow (bar) or 16th-note sine L/R swirl, keeping lows/mids centered and pulling amount down if motion distracts; or (B) duplicate synth+MIDI, mute alternating chord tones on each copy, and hard-pan L vs R so each side plays different notes of the same harmony—then confirm healthier correlation than chorus.
steps: Start from a good but narrow pad. Avoid broadband chorus/imager wideners (phasy/warbly, phase issues in lows/mids) and frequency stereo-spread (often not truly wide, can sound inside-out). Choose a method: A) high-band pan LFO on the same patch (steps 2–5), or B) interleaved chord split across two hard-panned layers (steps 6–9).
Method A: Insert multiband pan / band-limited auto-pan. Solo or target the high band only so lows stay centered.
Method A: Draw a sine (or subdued sine) pan path so highs slowly swirl L↔R. Try bar-length (4/4) for gentle immersion or 16th-note rate for more motion.
Method A: If 16ths feel too pronounced: switch to a less extreme pan profile and/or lower overall mix/amount of the pan effect.
Method A: A/B before/after in context: pad should envelop more without the washy phase of chorus/imager on full-band signal.
Method B: Duplicate the synth instance with identical settings and copy the MIDI to both tracks.
Method B: On track A piano roll, mute every other note top→bottom; on track B mute the complementary set bottom→top so together they reconstruct the full chords but separately play different notes.
Method B: Hard-pan A fully left and B fully right; play together for maximum width.

Method B: Check a correlation/phase meter: split technique should sit near ~0 (very wide) without deep negative swings; compare vs chorus (often flangy + negative correlation) and spreader (weaker width).

variants.name: Mono-safe width tricks: a 100%-wet short room IR as a stealth widener with width trim and gain make-up, a drawn and smoothed auto-pan rhythm, and Haas kept ≤15 ms split across bands tilted in opposite directions
variants.goal: Widen one headline element so it still works in mono. (1) Stealth IR widener: convolution with a short, thin-room impulse at 100% wet and decay down to ~20% so there is no audible tail. It widens and re-colours the chords. Because width makes the part quieter in mono, trim stereo width to ~65% and add ~+6.5 dB to match levels instead of lowering the mix. (2) Rhythmic auto-pan: start ~50% amount, then draw a stepped pan curve that fits the arp, round it with smoothing, optionally switch to unsynced Hz set by ear, and add a touch of multiband treble reverb before the panner. (3) Haas without the lopsided, phasey mono sum: keep the L/R delay ≤15 ms, tune it while listening in mono, tilt a mid band to one side and the treble band to the other, then reduce width and re-level. Use it on incidental FX rather than lead vocals. Use width with restraint so the one wide element stands out. Delta vs our Haas/phase-offset, high-band pan and asymmetric L/R skills: the IR widener with width trim, drawn pan rhythm, and opposite-tilt multiband Haas.
steps: Insert convolution reverb on the chords at 100% wet with a short, thin room IR and decay reduced to ~20% so no tail is heard. Audition other short IRs for different timbres.
Sum to mono: the widened chords drop in level. Instead of lowering the wet mix, follow with a width control at ~65% and raise gain ~6.5 dB to level-match.

Rhythmic pan for arps/synths: auto-pan at ~50% amount, try LFO shapes, then draw a custom stepped pan curve and add smoothing to round its edges. Optionally switch rate to unsynced Hz and set by ear to fit the part.
Add a touch of multiband treble-only reverb before the panner for air; adjust pan mix lower for just a flutter, or full for strong L/R jumps.
Haas: duplicate L/R with a delay on one side. Keep it at ≤15 ms and tune it while listening in mono until acceptable.
Fix the lopsided tilt: split into bands, tilt the mid band to the right and the treble band to the left, then reduce width and re-level.
Apply these to one headline sound (incidental FX/ear candy for Haas) while keeping most of the mix centred.

variants.name: Perceived width from narrow↔wide juxtaposition, real double-tracked (not cloned) hard pans, and a mono-safe stereo bed: mid-side EQ that nearly kills the mids on a send, plus reverb that decorrelates only the sides while the dry center stays untouched
variants.goal: Make a mix feel dramatically wide without master-bus wideners or phase-wrecked lows: write and arrange moments that open from narrower sections (juxtaposition), pan two real performances of the same part L/R (not a flipped copy), and for bass/beds use mid-side processing so the center stays dry and mono while only the sides get EQ lift and reverb. Delta vs stereo-width cluster: treats width as an arrangement/timing contrast first, insists on true double-tracks for L/R pan width, and the concrete M/S recipe of ~−30 dB mid cut on a parallel path plus dry-center / wet-sides reverb for mono-compatible stereo bass.
steps: Audit the arrangement: if everything is always wide, listeners adapt and nothing feels immersive. Plan narrower (near-mono) sections that precede the wide moments so the spread reads as a change.

For L/R width on a featured layer (e.g. vocals, guitars): use two real performances or differently processed takes of the same line and pan them apart (source example ~30 either way). A/B against a hard-panned clone of one take — the clone will not create the same image.

Build a mono-safe stereo bed for bass or a dense layer: send or parallel-process through a mid-side EQ and cut the mid channel hard (source: about −30 dB) so almost only sides remain on that path; optionally lift selected side bands. The dry center path keeps the mono power.
Feed that sides-heavy path into a reverb so the sides gain space while the middle stays completely dry and raw — mono fold-down still has the dry center.
Optional: light sidechain from drums into competing wide layers so mono-focused hits still punch. Check the whole mix in mono.
